chunks: But he who has done good things and believes, will have no fear of either being wronged or deprived.
ai.seo_question: What does a believer fear no injustice or loss?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of divine justice, assuring that the righteous are protected from the arbitrary deprivation of their due rewards by Allah. It underscores the psychological tranquility (sakina) derived from the certainty that one's faith and deeds are preserved in the Preserved Tablet, free from the fear of unjust loss.
